title: Algebraic stacks satisfy Rim–Schlessinger infinitesimal gluing
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and use schemes in the universes of [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Write $\mathcal X(T)$ for its fibre groupoid on an $S$-scheme $T$. A commutative local ring has a unique maximal ideal, and an Artinian ring satisfies the descending chain condition on ideals. For every pushout $T'=T\amalg_Z Z'$ in $S$-schemes in which all four schemes are spectra of Artinian local rings and are of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $Z\to Z'$ is a closed immersion defined by a nilpotent ideal, the restriction functor
$$\mathcal X(T')\longrightarrow\mathcal X(T)\times_{\mathcal X(Z)}\mathcal X(Z')$$
is an equivalence of groupoids. The groupoid on the right consists of triples $(a,b,\phi:a|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}b|_Z)$, with arrows pairs of isomorphisms commuting with $\phi$; the functor uses the canonical pullback comparison. No finite type or separation hypothesis on $\mathcal X\to S$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07WQ (lemma-algebraic-stack-RS), with condition (RS) of Tag 07WP (definition-RS). Affine Noetherian base specialization.

proof.text: Put $P=T'$. The map $Z\to T$ is affine, since both schemes are affine. Write $Z'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A'/I)$, with $I^N=0$. Every prime of $A'$ contains $I$: if $x\in I$, then $x^N=0$ lies in the prime, so primality gives $x$ in it. The quotient-spectrum homeomorphism therefore makes $Z\to Z'$ a thickening. The geometric pushout theorem identifies the given scheme pushout $P$ with the algebraic-space pushout of $T$ and $Z'$ along $Z$, and makes $T\to P$ a thickening. All identifications fix the original cocone maps, by uniqueness of pushouts.

source.place: Tags 07WQ (lemma-algebraic-stack-RS), 07WN (lemma-pushout), and 07SY (scheme pushouts are space pushouts).

proof.text: We will also use this universal property after every flat scheme map $B\to P$. Set $T_B=B\times_PT$, $Z'_B=B\times_PZ'$, $Z_B=B\times_PZ$. The flat counit of scheme pushout patching says exactly that $B$ is the scheme pushout $T_B\amalg_{Z_B}Z'_B$. The map $Z_B\to Z'_B$ is a thickening by base change, and $Z_B\to T_B$ is affine by affine base change. Thus the geometric pushout theorem makes this square a pushout for algebraic-space targets too. This argument requires no finite-presentation hypothesis on $B\to P$.

source.place: Tag 07WN full-faithfulness argument; Tag 07RX (lemma-equivalence-categories-schemes-over-pushout-flat), flat counit; Tag 07SY. Expanded flat-base version.

proof.text: The etale-stack convention for $\mathcal X$ has fppf descent by the smooth-atlas descent theorem. For any flat $B\to P$ and $c,d\in\mathcal X(B)$, that theorem also identifies $I=\operatorname{Isom}_B(c,d)$ as an algebraic space over $B$. Compatible isomorphisms on $T_B$ and $Z'_B$ are compatible sections of $I$ on those schemes. Step 2 glues their underlying maps uniquely to $s:B\to I$. Its composite to $B$ restricts to the original cocone maps, so the same pushout uniqueness, now with target $B$, gives $s$ a section. This establishes bijectivity on every isomorphism set, hence full faithfulness of the restriction functor for every flat $B\to P$, including $B=P$.

source.place: Tag 07WN (lemma-pushout), first paragraph, with Isom(c,d) for arbitrary objects; algebraic.tex Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal), criteria.tex Tag 076V.

proof.text: Fix a triple $(a,b,\phi)$ as in the statement and choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X$. By its definition, $V=T\times_{a,\mathcal X}U$ and $W=Z'\times_{b,\mathcal X}U$ are algebraic spaces smooth and surjective over $T,Z'$. Their objects over a test scheme consist of a base map, a map to $U$, and an isomorphism to the pulled-back object $a$ or $b$. Composing that isomorphism with $\phi$ identifies $V\times_TZ$ with $W\times_{Z'}Z$; call this common space $H$. This identification retains the map to $U$, so the two projections $H\to U$ agree. Smoothness gives flatness and local finite presentation of both $V\to T$ and $W\to Z'$.

source.place: Tag 07WN, second paragraph: pull back a smooth atlas and use the given isomorphism to identify the restrictions.

proof.text: Form the geometric pushout $V'=V\amalg_HW$. Its canonical restrictions to $T,Z'$ recover $V,W$, with precisely the chosen identification over $Z$. The theorem also makes $V\to V'$ a thickening. Since the maps $V\to U$ and $W\to U$ agree on $H$, the pushout universal property produces a unique map $V'\to U$. Only these stated geometric properties of the pushout are used here; the flat scheme chart in the next step will provide the covering needed for descent.

source.place: Tag 07WN, construction of the pushout and its map to the atlas; Tag 07VX/07W0. Only geometric pushout recovery is used here.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $V_1\to V$. The compatible-chart theorem supplies a surjective etale scheme chart $W_1\to W$, an identified overlap $H_1=V_1\times_TZ\cong W_1\times_{Z'}Z$, and a scheme $E=V_1\amalg_{H_1}W_1$ with a surjective etale map $E\to V'$. The maps $V_1\to T$ and $W_1\to Z'$ are smooth by composition of an etale map with a smooth map; hence they are flat and locally finitely presented. Scheme pushout patching therefore says $E\to P$ is flat and locally finitely presented. The maps $T\to P$ and $V\to V'$ are thickenings, so their maps on point spaces are onto; since $V\to T$ is surjective, $V'\to P$ is surjective. Consequently $E\to P$ is surjective as well and is an fppf covering. This is why no additional smooth-pushout lemma is needed.

source.place: Tag 07WN, last paragraph, choosing a scheme cover of the patched atlas; spaces-pushouts.tex Tags 07W0/07W2 and more-morphisms.tex Tag 07RX(3). It suffices to obtain an fppf cover, without asserting smoothness of the pushout.

proof.text: Pull the atlas object in $\mathcal X(U)$ back along $E\to V'\to U$, obtaining $c\in\mathcal X(E)$. By the defining triple description of $V,W$, their tautological isomorphisms identify the restrictions of $c$ to $E\times_PT$ and $E\times_PZ'$ with the restrictions of $a,b$. On $E\times_PZ$ those identifications commute with $\phi$, because the identification of $H$ was defined by composition with $\phi$ and the pushout recovery maps preserve it. Thus $c$ maps to the specified triple over $E$, with an isomorphism of triples, not just equality of isomorphism classes.

source.place: Tag 07WN, final paragraph: the atlas object and its two compatible restrictions. Explicit pullback of the object replaces an invocation of 2-Yoneda.

proof.text: On $E_2=E\times_PE$, the two pullbacks of $c$ have images canonically isomorphic through the fixed triple $(a,b,\phi)$. The map $E_2\to P$ is flat, and likewise $E_3=E\times_PE\times_PE\to P$ is flat, by base change and composition of flat maps. Step 3 therefore lifts the isomorphism on $E_2$ uniquely to an isomorphism between those pullbacks of $c$. Its inverse and its cocycle equality on $E_3$ follow by faithfulness, since their images are the inverse and cocycle of the fixed triple. Effective fppf descent yields $c_0\in\mathcal X(P)$. The compatible identifications with $a$ and $b$ descend along the base changes of the fppf cover $E\to P$, using the fppf sheaf property for isomorphisms. Their compatibility with $\phi$ is an equality of sections and holds after that cover, hence holds globally. Thus $c_0$ maps to the given triple. Essential surjectivity together with Step 3 proves the equivalence. No finiteness or separation of $\mathcal X\to S$ was used.

source.place: Tag 07WN, local essential surjectivity and descent, expanding the argument of stacks.tex Tag 046N (lemma-characterize-essentially-surjective-when-ff).

proof_origin.place: Tags 07WQ and 07WN (lemma-algebraic-stack-RS and lemma-pushout), expanded by compatible scheme charts 07W0/07W2 and flat scheme patching 07RX(3). The final atlas cover need only be fppf.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q93-8ec223581 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the 8-step split of 07WQ in full. The proof expands Stacks 07WN (artin.tex lemma-pushout), which I read with its proof. There are no new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the live version. The added 'nilpotent ideal' hypothesis is automatic for local Artinian spectra, so the target is not weakened. The item is not superseded (live status: unsplit), there is no re-split note, and there is no cycle. Step checks: (1) the space-pushout node applies with the thickening Z→Z' (via 00E5 and the nilpotent-prime argument) and the affine map Z→T (01SH). It makes P the space pushout and T→P a thickening. (2) The flat-W clause of the flat-patching node (07RX), together with thickening base change and affine base change, makes every flat B over P a space pushout. (3) Isom_B(c,d) is an algebraic space; gluing sections of it gives full faithfulness for every flat B. (4)-(5) Atlas pullbacks V and W over T and Z', identified through phi; the pushout V' has its recovery isomorphisms and a map V'→U. (6) Compatible étale charts (07W0/07W2) give a scheme E. V_1→T and W_1→Z' are smooth, so flat patching makes E→P flat and lfp; surjectivity comes from the thickening homeomorphism. So E→P is an fppf cover. This replaces the 07W3 smoothness of V' with exactly what descent needs. (7) The pulled-back atlas object gives an isomorphism of triples over E. (8) Descent datum by flat full faithfulness on E2/E3, effective fppf descent, and descent of the identifications with a, b and phi. Edge cases checked: the k⊂k[ε] square and the dual-number fibre-product square. Duplicate grep for 07WN/07WQ/RS: none. lean.note: Total-category formulation of the canonical fibre restriction equivalence: every span over the overlap with its specified lifted arrows extends to a pushout over the given base pushout. In a category fibred in groupoids this retains precisely the compatible triples and their isomorphisms; the pushout universal property includes full faithfulness. All four Artinian-local and finite-type conditions are retained. No statement correction.
